body:
Part of the **Veles OTP external devices** RFC execution plan (OTP-24).

Production headless plain-Rust host implementing `hello`, `start_scan`, `stop_scan`, `connect`, `disconnect`, `send`, `shutdown` and emitting `ready`, `device_found`, `scan_state`, `connected`, `disconnected`, `sent`, `message`, `shutdown_complete`, `error`; strict versioning, request correlation, process-local handles, WinRT/CoreBluetooth adapters, bridge-owned GATT fragmentation/reassembly, bounded ephemeral state, safe errors, cleanup. No persistence, no product UI, no OTP/trust interpretation, no network/listener/autostart.

**Full task specification:** see section `### OTP-24` in the RFC: docs/rfcs/2026-08-21-otp-external-devices.md (PR #79) — https://github.com/raidenyn/veles-android/pull/79

## OTP-23 carried-forward verification obligations


Tracking amendment from the post-grant review of #86 / PR #123 (baseline `cab043885ffe1991a6f3037c69a768ed6acbcd00`). These checklists assign future implementation/retest ownership; they do **not** mark a test PASS, waive a requirement, change dependencies, or authorize OTP-24. The current OTP-23 decision remains NO-GO until an explicit owner-approved gate amendment or satisfaction of its criteria. Only new-account W-01/M-01/M-02 are waived as nonblocking NOT RUN. Preserve earlier failed evidence and stable signing identities.

### Host implementation acceptance (primary owner: this issue)
- [ ] **W-02 / M-08:** observe host and launcher/wrapper window state and communication endpoints at ready, during active scans, during two-phone connected transfers, and after teardown. Record measured vs unavailable fields; startup-only counts are insufficient. Target is the selected plain-Rust runtime, not a Tauri event loop.
- [ ] **W-07 / W-08:** with an active scan and two byte-proven links, separately exercise literal Chrome `port.disconnect()`, tab close, stdin EOF, truncated-frame EOF, and shutdown. Capture last output, stdout closure, process/wrapper exit, released links and survivor isolation. Distinguish direct-process EOF from Chrome-owned-port provenance; failed setup is not a teardown PASS.
- [ ] Turn the early Windows `access_denied` investigation in #86 into regression coverage for any established root cause. Record incidental failures and retry behavior; do not hide them behind a successful retry.
- [ ] Test classified unavailable-adapter, Bluetooth-off and access-denied paths plus bounded reconnect/cleanup; coordinate the controlled physical interruption matrix with #102.
Closure evidence links to connector checks in #88 and production-shaped Gate B checks in #94. The early architecture questions remain owned by #86, rather than being silently deferred here.

comments.body:
Execution-plan update in **#123** (prerequisite #122): the selected production runtime is **plain Rust without the Tauri event loop**. Packaging-only Tauri retention is not approved or justified by the current comparison; OTP-25 selects another pipeline or brings a separately reviewed justification.

The explicit latest OTP-23 disposition is **NO-GO**. Fresh single-phone Windows exchanges through 4096 bytes support the revised contract, but two-phone concurrency/failure isolation, full active-link cleanup, strict background evidence, M6 and macOS permission/signing/recovery requirements are still unmet. The user-approved new-account test waiver is explicit and non-blocking; the remaining criteria are not waived.

No OTP-24 implementation is included. Keep this task blocked on OTP-23; CI green on #123 is a software gate, not protected-transport eligibility.

## OTP-23 prerequisite update — still NO-GO

PR #123 now contains the post-grant two-phone, concurrency, lifecycle, background and macOS permission-recovery evidence plus the independent review/fix verification. Several measured transport criteria now pass, including the scoped M6 phone-clock adjudication.

**This does not authorize OTP-24 implementation.** The acceptance matrix still has required blockers: signing provenance, existing-account unsigned-host matrix, connected-phase window evidence, incomplete Windows port/EOF/radio cases, macOS guidance/prompt ownership, physical duplicate-connect/ordering proof, and the literal background timer-exemption condition. Historical macOS background PASS adjudications used an earlier evaluator; current re-evaluations remain BLOCKED for missing foreground evidence. No acceptance requirement was silently revised.

Only W-01/M-01/M-02 (new-account tests) retain the user-approved nonblocking `NOT RUN` waiver. Plain Rust remains the selected runtime; packaging-only Tauri retention is not approved. #86 and this issue remain open; #123 remains unmerged pending its prerequisite and review.
